title: Kernel fusion playbook + reading notes
content:
Quick goal: collect reading notes + an experiment playbook for evaluating unified kernel fusion strategies across our fleet (A100/MI300/H100 mix). This is a personal scratchpad — informal, lots of TODOs, rough commands, hypothesis-driven experiments.

TL;DR notes from papers/blogs (very rough):
- Kernel-Fuse-2025 (conf/arch) - show that combining pointwise and matmul loops into single kernels reduces memory writebacks and improves cuBLAS handoffs. Key takeaway: fusion wins when intermediate tensors are > L2 capacity but < L3; benefits shrink as register pressure increases.
K-Fuse auto-tuner blog (2026) - autotune heuristics that pick fusion candidates by cost-modeling L2 spill vs recompute. They use tiny microbenchmarks per operator pair and cache the decision per shape/dtype. Good inspiration for a lightweight on-node cache.
Mixed-Kernel-Dispatch (2024) - scheduling mixed-fused vs dedicated kernels depending on occupancy. Important: scheduling policy should consider multi-tenant interference and batch-size distribution.

Personal synthesis (what I think matters for Redwood):
- Our runtime has to pick kernels with three axes in mind: latency-SLOs (p95), token throughput (tokens/s), and cost (GPU-hours / token). Fusion can trade throughput for lower p95 by reducing global memory traffic, but may increase tail latency if it triggers register spills or reduces SM occupancy.
- Heterogeneous fleet problem: an H100 baseline might benefit from deeper fusion (higher register use is OK), but MI300 might prefer shallower fusion because of different vector widths and memory hierarchy. Need model recipes per device family.

Open questions (quick):
- How do fused kernels affect checkpointing KV cache boundaries? If a fused kernel spans layers we usually break to manage KV cache persistency, could complicate streaming generation fallback.
- How big is the dev/ops cost of maintaining fused-kernel variants per model config vs relying on compiler-level fusion (e.g., Triton auto-fusion)?
- Are there quantization interactions? early experiments suggest fused kernels that assume int8 elementwise introduce different scaling reconstruction costs.

Reading snippets / bookmarks (links + one-liners):
- https://arxiv.org/abs/xxxx.xxxxx - "Fusion for Transformers": formalizes memory-latency model; useful for cost function.
- https://engineering.blog/k-fuse - practical autotuner blog; consider local microbenchmark + canonical cache.
- https://github.com/KFuse/benchmarks - microbench harness (copy locally and adapt).

Experiment plan (milestones):
- Stage 0: microbench harness on a single node (H100). Reproduce K-Fuse microbench for matmul+gelu + matmul+layernorm combos. Collect: latency distribution (50/90/95/99), peak memory, flops, occupancy.
  - commands: python bench.py --op pair --shapes "[[1,1024,4096],[1,4096,1024]]" --dtype float16 --reps 2000 
  - quick parse: jq .results | csv -> pandas for plotting
- Stage 1: small LLM end-to-end (LlamaX-13B) with synthetic inputs to see p50/p95 tokens/s with fusion toggled. Use perf markers in runtime.
  - run: ./run_serving_local --model llamaX-13b --batching disabled --fusion-mode on/off --trace out/fuse-trace.json
- Stage 2: multi-tenant interference test. Run 2x medium streams + 4x small chat streams; check queuing / queuing-time + p95.
- Stage 3: automated autotuner prototype. Given microbench results, generate rule table keyed by (device_family, op_pair, shape_heuristic, dtype) -> fuse|no_fuse. Start with simple heuristics and add a small LR/regression model if needed.

Metrics to collect (per experiment):
- tokens/s, p50/p95 latency per token, GPU utilization, SM occupancy, memory bandwidth (NVLINK/HPB where applicable), peak rss on host, compilation time (for JIT kernels), kernel launch overhead.

Quick results notes from preliminary runs (H100 local VM; tiny sample):
- matmul+gelu fusion reduced global memory traffic by ~22% for hidden dim 4096 at bs1, improved p95 token latency by ~12% but increased single-kernel wall time by 5% (fewer launches).
- On MI300 emulation (via vendor sim), fusion policies that use more registers throttle concurrency and hurt small-batch throughput; need to preserve multi-warp concurrency.

Failure modes to watch:
- OOM when fusion decision doesn't account for KV cache spikes during generation.
- Regression in streaming SLOs because fusion reduces ability to preempt long kernels (long fused kernels block low-latency small requests).
- Compiling fused kernels increases cold-start time for new model versions (affects canary rollouts).

Implementation sketch (runtime hooks):
- Add a FusionDecision module in kernel_selector: inputs: op_graph_window (n layers, ops), device_meta (family, L2 size, regs_per_sm), workload_profile (batch distribution, seq_len distribution), constraints (max_kernel_length, latency_SLO_breakdown). Output: {plan_id, fuse_windows}. Cache this decision per model-version + device_family.
- Simple default: prefer no-fuse for sequences < 512 and batch > 4; prefer shallow fusion for seq 512-2048; prefer deep fusion for seq > 2048 on H100. (TBD after microbench).

TODOs (immediate):
- [ ] Port K-Fuse microbench scripts to our infra and standardize output JSON (Ravi).
- [ ] Add trace markers for fused kernels in runtime (Mika).
- [ ] Run baseline microbench on one MI300 and one H100 node with identical shapes (me).
- [ ] Draft a short canary play for fusion rollouts that includes a fast rollback path when p95 regresses (Kendra).

Notes to self (random):
- Keep experiment names consistent: use fugue-<device>-<op>-<shape>-<date> for artifact naming. 
- Slack thread: #runtime-kernels -> summarize and pin most useful graphs.

Random scribbles / heuristics for the autotuner (brainstorm):
- cost = alpha * p95 + beta * (1/tokens_per_sec) + gamma * compile_time_penalty + delta * memory_spill_risk
- memory_spill_risk estimated via (register_usage_estimate > threshold) OR (L2_bandwidth / expected_memory_writeback < epsilon)
- prefer microbench aggregated over 3 seeds, median of medians.

End notes: this is rough. Want to keep momentum on small wins (microbench reproduction first). When we have reproducible delta > 8-10% p95 or tokens/s improvements on 13B/7B baselines, write a short internal note for product about applicability (Dedicated customers might prefer deeper fusion knobs in their config).

Link backlog:
- GH bench fork: https://github.com/cassie-moreno/k-fuse-fork (private)
- Jira RINF-1289 (tuning rules)
- Slack: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C0RUNTIME (reference)

Scratch-of-ideas for a future doc: "Kernel fusion playbook for customer tiers" -> include recommended default policy per tier (hosted/dedicated/private).

-- cassie
